items.title: Allen–Cahn and Cahn–Hilliard double-well gradient flows
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, let $d\ge1$, and fix constants $\varepsilon>0$, $M>0$, and $\kappa>0$. Put
$$F_\varepsilon(s)=\frac{(s^2-1)^2}{4\varepsilon^2},\qquad f_\varepsilon(s)=F_\varepsilon'(s)=\frac{s^3-s}{\varepsilon^2},$$
and define the free energy on $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)\cap L^4(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ by
$$\mathcal E_\varepsilon(u)=\int_\Omega\left(\frac{\kappa}{2}|\nabla u|^2+F_\varepsilon(u)\right)\,dx.$$
Here $H^1=W^{1,2}$ and weak derivatives have the meaning in [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The finite-energy initial class consists of $u_0\in H^1(\Omega)\cap L^4(\Omega)$.

The **Allen–Cahn gradient flow** is
$$u_t=-M\mu,\qquad \mu=-\kappa\Delta u+f_\varepsilon(u),\qquad \partial_nu=0,\qquad u(0)=u_0.$$
The **Cahn–Hilliard gradient flow** is
$$u_t=M\Delta\mu,\qquad \mu=-\kappa\Delta u+f_\varepsilon(u),\qquad \partial_nu=\partial_n\mu=0,\qquad u(0)=u_0.$$
For weak solutions, the no-flux conditions are encoded by the natural weak formulations with all $H^1(\Omega)$ test functions. In dimensions $d\ge5$, the finite-energy class $H^1\cap L^4$ alone does not in general make $f_\varepsilon(u)$ a continuous functional on $H^1(\Omega)$: it gives only $f_\varepsilon(u)\in L^{4/3}$, while $H^1(\Omega)$ need not embed into $L^4(\Omega)$. Thus any weak solution tested against all $H^1$ functions must have the additional integrability needed to make the nonlinear pairing continuous. The chemical potential $\mu$ is the variational derivative of $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$, and the mobilities select the $L^2$ metric for Allen–Cahn and the mean-zero $H^{-1}$ metric for Cahn–Hilliard. In the Cahn–Hilliard flow, the no-flux equation conserves $\int_\Omega u$; the Allen–Cahn flow has no such conservation law in general. No maximum-principle property is part of these definitions.

The convergence theorem on this page is restricted to one space dimension. Assuming the Axiom of Choice for the following standard embedding consequences, if $d=2$ and $\Omega$ is a bounded $W^{1,p}$ extension domain for every $1<p<2$ as defined in [[def-sobolev-extension-domain-and-extension-operator]], then [[thm-critical-sobolev-embedding-into-every-finite-lq]] gives $H^1(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^4(\Omega)$. If $d=3$ and $\Omega$ is a bounded $W^{1,2}$ extension domain, then [[thm-sobolev-embedding-on-bounded-extension-domains-for-p-less-than-n]] gives $H^1(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^4(\Omega)$. These are the exact extra extension hypotheses for the quartic-energy claim. In dimensions $d\ge4$ no assertion that every $H^1$ state has finite quartic energy is made; the explicit initial class above remains $H^1\cap L^4$. No sharp-interface limit as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ is part of either definition.

items.title: Kernel, range, and mean-zero inverse for the no-flux Laplacian
items.statement:
Use either connected no-flux realization in [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]]. In its finite-volume branch, assume the interior cell graph is connected; in its interval conforming branch, assume $N\ge1$. Write $\bar u_h=\langle u_h,\mathbf1\rangle_h/\langle\mathbf1,\mathbf1\rangle_h$ and $X_{h,0}=\{u_h:\bar u_h=0\}$. Then $A_h$ is self-adjoint and nonnegative, $\ker A_h=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}$, and $\operatorname{ran}A_h=X_{h,0}$. The restriction $A_h:X_{h,0}\to X_{h,0}$ is positive definite and invertible. Define $A_h^\dagger u_h$ by first projecting $u_h$ onto $X_{h,0}$ and then applying this self-adjoint positive inverse. For each fixed finite mesh there is $C_h<\infty$ such that
$$\|u_h-\bar u_h\mathbf1\|_h^2\le C_h\langle A_hu_h,u_h\rangle_h.$$
For a one-cell mesh, $X_{h,0}=\{0\}$ and the inequality is vacuous.
items.strategy: Use the symmetric energy form and connectedness to identify the kernel; use rank-nullity for the range and inverse; minimize the positive Rayleigh quotient on the mean-zero sphere for the mesh-dependent bound.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; all spaces are finite-dimensional.

items.title: Uniform interval stability of the phase-field L2 projector
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=(0,L)$ and let $V_h$ be the conforming interval space in [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]], with center spacing $h$. Let $I_hv$ interpolate the absolutely-continuous representative of $v\in H^1(0,L)$ at the centers and extend it constantly to the two boundary half-cells. Let $P_h$ be the exact $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto $V_h$. There is a constant $C$ independent of $h$ such that
$$\|I_hv\|_{H^1}\le C\|v\|_{H^1},\qquad \|v-I_hv\|_{L^2}\le Ch\|v'\|_{L^2},\qquad \|P_hv\|_{H^1}\le C\|v\|_{H^1}.$$
In addition, $\|P_hv-v\|_{L^2}\le Ch\|v'\|_{L^2}$ for every $v\in H^1(0,L)$, $P_hv\to v$ in $H^1(0,L)$ for every $v\in H^1(0,L)$, and $P_hg\to g$ in $L^2(0,L)$ for every $g\in L^2(0,L)$ as $h\to0$.
items.strategy: Derive interpolation error and an inverse estimate, combine them with L2 contraction for uniform H1 stability, prove smooth H1 approximation, and extend by density to every H1 function.
items.axiom_base: Assume the Axiom of Choice through the supplier providing the unique absolutely-continuous representative of each one-dimensional H1 class, so nodal interpolation is well-defined; its Countable Choice consequence also supplies smooth L2 approximants for the density argument.

items.title: Stabilized semi-implicit phase-field step
items.statement:
On either discrete realization of [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]], write $X_h=\mathbb R^{\mathcal K}$ for the finite-volume state space and $X_h=V_h$ for the conforming interval state space; use its inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_h$ and the energy components $E_{c,h},E_{e,h}$ defined there. Let $g_h(u)=\nabla_h(E_{c,h}-E_{e,h})(u)$ be the Riesz gradient of the full potential energy. In the finite-volume realization, $(g_h(u))_K=f_\varepsilon(u_K)$. In the conforming interval realization, $g_h(u)\in V_h$ is defined by
$$\langle g_h(u),v_h\rangle_h=\int_0^L f_\varepsilon(u_h(x))v_h(x)\,dx\qquad(v_h\in V_h),$$
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_h$ is the exact $L^2$ inner product. Given a previous state $u^n\in X_h$, parameters $\varepsilon,\kappa,M,\tau>0$, and a stabilization parameter $S\ge0$, the **stabilized semi-implicit Allen–Cahn step** is the linear equation
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M\left(\kappa A_hu^{n+1}+g_h(u^n)+S(u^{n+1}-u^n)\right).$$
For the same input, the **stabilized semi-implicit Cahn–Hilliard step** is
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M A_h\mu^{n+1},\qquad \mu^{n+1}=\kappa A_hu^{n+1}+g_h(u^n)+S(u^{n+1}-u^n).$$
These formulas define alternative updates with an explicitly lagged nonlinear potential and an added increment term. No energy law, unconditional solvability, maximum principle, or error estimate is asserted here for the quartic double well; any such property requires its own hypotheses and proof. In particular, no stability estimate proved for the convex-splitting update is silently transferred to this variant.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691

The paper writes its stabilization as $S/\varepsilon^2$ and takes unit mobility and stiffness; the definition here permits general $M,\kappa$ and defines its own coefficient $S$. The source's stability statements require the hypotheses stated there and are not imported.

items.title: First-order scalar-auxiliary-variable Cahn–Hilliard step
items.statement:
Use either Cahn–Hilliard realization of [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]]. Write $X_h=\mathbb R^{\mathcal K}$ for the finite-volume state space and $X_h=V_h$ for the conforming interval state space; use the specified inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_h$ in each case. Set $E_{1,h}=E_{c,h}-E_{e,h}$. Since $F_\varepsilon(s)=(s^2-1)^2/(4\varepsilon^2)\ge0$, this is nonnegative. Explicitly,
$$E_{1,h}(u)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|F_\varepsilon(u_K)\quad\text{in the finite-volume realization},$$
and
$$E_{1,h}(u_h)=\int_0^L F_\varepsilon(u_h(x))\,dx\quad\text{in the conforming interval realization}.$$
Its Riesz gradient $g_{1,h}(u)=\nabla_hE_{1,h}(u)$ is specified in the finite-volume realization by $(g_{1,h}(u))_K=f_\varepsilon(u_K)$, where $f_\varepsilon=F_\varepsilon'$. In the conforming interval realization it is the unique $g_{1,h}(u_h)\in V_h$ satisfying
$$\langle g_{1,h}(u),v_h\rangle_h=\int_0^L f_\varepsilon(u_h(x))v_h(x)\,dx\qquad(v_h\in V_h),$$
with the exact $L^2$ inner product from that realization.

**Inputs:** $u^n\in X_h$, $r^n\in\mathbb R$, and parameters $\varepsilon,\kappa,M,\tau,C_0>0$. Set $\alpha_n=(E_{1,h}(u^n)+C_0)^{-1/2}$. **Output:** the tuple $(u^{n+1},r^{n+1},\mu^{n+1})$ obtained by solving the linear equations
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M A_h\mu^{n+1},$$
$$\mu^{n+1}=\kappa A_hu^{n+1}+\alpha_n r^{n+1}g_{1,h}(u^n),$$
$$r^{n+1}-r^n=\frac{\alpha_n}{2}\langle g_{1,h}(u^n),u^{n+1}-u^n\rangle_h.$$
The initial scalar may be set to $r^0=\sqrt{E_{1,h}(u^0)+C_0}$. After a step, $r^{n+1}$ is an independent auxiliary variable determined by the third equation; the scheme does not impose $r^{n+1}=\sqrt{E_{1,h}(u^{n+1})+C_0}$.

items.title: Backward-Euler convex splitting for Allen–Cahn and Cahn–Hilliard
items.statement:
Let $X_h$ be either finite-dimensional realization in [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]], with real inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_h$, constant vector $\mathbf1$, self-adjoint nonnegative $A_h$ with kernel $\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}$, and $A_h^\dagger$ from [[lem-phase-field-neumann-laplacian-kernel-and-gauge]]. Let $P_{c,h},P_{e,h}:X_h\to\mathbb R$ be the differentiable convex energy components specified there; $\nabla_hP$ denotes the Riesz gradient relative to $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_h$. Put
$$\mathcal E_h(u)=\frac\kappa2\langle A_hu,u\rangle_h+P_{c,h}(u)-P_{e,h}(u),\qquad \mu_h(u,v)=\kappa A_hu+\nabla_hP_{c,h}(u)-\nabla_hP_{e,h}(v).$$
Given $u^n\in X_h$, $\tau>0$, and $M>0$, the backward-Euler convex-splitting step is:

1. **Allen–Cahn branch.** Return the minimizer over $v\in X_h$ of
$$J_{AC}(v)=\frac{1}{2M\tau}\|v-u^n\|_h^2+\frac\kappa2\langle A_hv,v\rangle_h+P_{c,h}(v)-\langle\nabla_hP_{e,h}(u^n),v\rangle_h,$$
and set $\mu^{n+1}=\mu_h(u^{n+1},u^n)$.

2. **Cahn–Hilliard branch.** Restrict to the affine set $\langle v,\mathbf1\rangle_h=\langle u^n,\mathbf1\rangle_h$ and return the minimizer of
$$J_{CH}(v)=\frac{1}{2M\tau}\langle A_h^\dagger(v-u^n),v-u^n\rangle_h+\frac\kappa2\langle A_hv,v\rangle_h+P_{c,h}(v)-\langle\nabla_hP_{e,h}(u^n),v\rangle_h,$$
then set $\mu^{n+1}=\mu_h(u^{n+1},u^n)$.

For the finite-volume realization, $P_{c,h}(u)=\sum_K|K|F_c(u_K)$ and $P_{e,h}(u)=\sum_K|K|F_e(u_K)$. For the conforming interval realization, these are the exact integrals of $F_c$ and $F_e$ over the reconstructed piecewise-affine state. The recurrence, minimizer equivalence, uniqueness, conservation, and energy bounds are proved in [[thm-phase-field-convex-splitting-step-existence-and-energy]]. This is the selected backward-Euler branch; it asserts no ARS(2,2,2), Lie, or Strang property.

items.title: The SAV step is uniquely solvable and dissipates a modified energy
items.statement:
Under the finite-dimensional hypotheses of [[alg-phase-field-sav-cahn-hilliard-step]], the displayed SAV linear system has a unique solution at every step. Every solution conserves the discrete mean and obeys
$$\widetilde E_h(u^{n+1},r^{n+1})+\frac\kappa2\langle A_h\delta u,\delta u\rangle_h+(\delta r)^2+M\tau\langle A_h\mu^{n+1},\mu^{n+1}\rangle_h=\widetilde E_h(u^n,r^n),$$
where $\delta u=u^{n+1}-u^n$, $\delta r=r^{n+1}-r^n$, and
$$\widetilde E_h(u,r)=\frac\kappa2\langle A_hu,u\rangle_h+r^2.$$
Thus $\widetilde E_h$ is nonincreasing. This conclusion is about the modified energy; it does not assert monotonicity of the original physical energy $\mathcal E_h(u)=\frac\kappa2\langle A_hu,u\rangle_h+E_{1,h}(u)$.
items.strategy: Show the homogeneous linear SAV system has trivial kernel, then pair the three update equations to derive conservation and the exact modified-energy identity.

items.title: Existence, uniqueness, mass conservation, and energy decay of a convex-splitting step
items.statement:
Use the finite-dimensional realization and the hypotheses of [[alg-phase-field-convex-splitting-backward-euler]]. Assume $P_{c,h}$ is convex and coercive on $X_h$, and $P_{e,h}$ is differentiable and convex. For every $u^n$, $M>0$, and $\tau>0$, both branches have a unique minimizer. Their first-order conditions are exactly
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M\mu^{n+1}\quad\text{(Allen–Cahn)},$$
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M A_h\mu^{n+1}\quad\text{(Cahn–Hilliard)}.$$
The Cahn–Hilliard branch conserves $\langle u^n,\mathbf1\rangle_h$. With $\mathcal E_h$ as in the algorithm,
$$\mathcal E_h(u^{n+1})+M\tau\|\mu^{n+1}\|_h^2\le\mathcal E_h(u^n)\quad\text{(Allen–Cahn)},$$
$$\mathcal E_h(u^{n+1})+M\tau\langle A_h\mu^{n+1},\mu^{n+1}\rangle_h\le\mathcal E_h(u^n)\quad\text{(Cahn–Hilliard)}.$$
For the quartic split in [[def-phase-field-gradient-flow-and-double-well]], the required convexity and coercivity hold for both realizations.
items.strategy: Establish quartic coercivity and convexity, minimize on the full or fixed-mean finite-dimensional domain, derive Euler equations, and apply convexity plus the update identity to obtain energy decay.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; minimizers are attained in finite-dimensional spaces by coercivity and finite-dimensional compactness.

items.title: First-order time error under smooth fixed-mesh solutions
items.statement:
Fix one finite-dimensional realization in [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]] and $T>0$. Let $G_{c,h}(u)=\kappa A_hu+\nabla_hP_{c,h}(u)$ and $G_{e,h}(u)=\nabla_hP_{e,h}(u)$. The exact semidiscrete Allen–Cahn trajectory is the solution of $y'=-M(G_{c,h}(y)-G_{e,h}(y))$; the exact semidiscrete Cahn–Hilliard trajectory is the fixed-mean solution of $y'=-MA_h(G_{c,h}(y)-G_{e,h}(y))$. Assume the applicable exact trajectory is $C^2$ on $[0,T]$ and remains in a compact set. Let the numerical solution start from $u^0=y(0)$ and use the convex-splitting step. Then there are constants $C>0$ and $\tau_0>0$, depending on the fixed spatial realization, $\varepsilon,\kappa,M$, the exact trajectory, and $T$, such that, for $0<\tau\le\tau_0$:

- for Allen–Cahn, $\max_{n\tau\le T}\|u^n-y(t_n)\|_h\le C\tau$;
- for Cahn–Hilliard, with $y$ and $u^n$ having the same mean and $\|z\|_{-1,h}^2=\langle A_h^\dagger z,z\rangle_h$ on mean-zero vectors, $\max_{n\tau\le T}\|u^n-y(t_n)\|_{-1,h}\le C\tau$.

This is a fixed-mesh time estimate; it is not a uniform spatial error bound.
items.strategy: Bound the backward-Euler residual and use monotonicity and discrete Gronwall in L2 for AC and the mean-zero H-1 inner product for CH.

items.title: One-dimensional mesh and time convergence of convex-splitting phase flows
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and use the separable Hilbert evolution triple $V=H^1(0,L)\Subset H=L^2(0,L)\hookrightarrow V^*$. Let $\Omega=(0,L)$, $T>0$, and use the conforming interval realization in [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]] with $h=L/N$ and time steps $\tau=T/J$, where $N,J\to\infty$. Fix $\varepsilon,\kappa,M>0$. For each $h,\tau$, initialize $u_h^0=P_hu_0$ with $u_0\in H^1(0,L)$ and use the corresponding convex-splitting scheme. Set $t_n=n\tau$ and, for $t\in(t_n,t_{n+1}]$, let $u_{h,\tau}(t)=u_h^{n+1}$, $\mu_{h,\tau}(t)=\mu_h^{n+1}$, and $D_\tau u_{h,\tau}(t)=(u_h^{n+1}-u_h^n)/\tau$; values at the finitely many endpoints do not affect the Bochner classes. There is a subsequence with $h,\tau\to0$ such that $u_{h,\tau}\to u$ strongly in $L^2((0,T)\times(0,L))$ and weakly in $L^2(0,T;H^1(0,L))$.

For the Allen–Cahn branch, the limit satisfies, for every $\phi\in C^1([0,T]\times[0,L])$ with $\phi(T,\cdot)=0$,
$$-\int_0^T\!\int_0^L u\,\partial_t\phi\,dxdt+M\kappa\int_0^T\!\int_0^L u_x\phi_x\,dxdt+M\int_0^T\!\int_0^L f_\varepsilon(u)\phi\,dxdt=\int_0^L u_0(x)\phi(0,x)\,dx.$$

For the Cahn–Hilliard branch, along a further subsequence $\mu_{h,\tau}\rightharpoonup\mu$ weakly in $L^2(0,T;H^1(0,L))$, and
$$-\int_0^T\!\int_0^L u\,\partial_t\phi\,dxdt+M\int_0^T\!\int_0^L \mu_x\phi_x\,dxdt=\int_0^L u_0(x)\phi(0,x)\,dx,$$
for every $\psi\in H^1(0,L)$ and $\eta\in L^2(0,T)$,
$$\int_0^T\eta(t)\left[\int_0^L\mu(t,x)\psi(x)\,dx-\kappa\int_0^L u_x(t,x)\psi_x(x)\,dx-\int_0^L f_\varepsilon(u(t,x))\psi(x)\,dx\right]dt=0,$$
and $\int_0^L u(t,x)\,dx=\int_0^L u_0(x)\,dx$ for almost every $t$. The no-flux boundary conditions are encoded by the $H^1$ test spaces. The quartic nonlinearity is controlled here by the one-dimensional embedding $H^1(0,L)\hookrightarrow L^\infty(0,L)$. This theorem is for fixed $\varepsilon$ and $d=1$; it does not assert a higher-dimensional finite-volume limit or an $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ sharp-interface result.
items.strategy: Derive uniform energy, chemical-potential, and time-derivative bounds; apply discrete Aubin–Lions and weak compactness; pass projected tests and the quartic nonlinearities to the limit.
items.axiom_base: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It is used by the PE12 discrete Aubin–Lions compactness theorem and by the weak subsequence extraction in the separable Bochner Hilbert supplier; the finite-dimensional step theorem is choice-free.

title: Phase-field and dissipative gradient-flow computation — Examples

items.title: The one-dimensional Allen–Cahn double-well front
items.statement:
For $\kappa,\varepsilon>0$, on the real line set
$$u_\varepsilon(x)=\tanh\!\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2\kappa}\,\varepsilon}\right).$$
This is a stationary finite-energy heteroclinic profile for the one-dimensional Allen–Cahn Euler–Lagrange equation $-\kappa u''+f_\varepsilon(u)=0$. It is a profile example on $\mathbb R$, not a boundary-value solution on a bounded no-flux interval.
items.strategy: Differentiate the tanh profile, verify the ODE exactly, and integrate its exponentially decaying energy density.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §1, equations (1.1)–(1.5), PDF pp. 1–2: the Allen–Cahn Euler–Lagrange equation and double-well model. The heteroclinic profile is verified directly here.

items.title: Interface width and a grid that misses the transition
items.statement:
For the front in [[ex-phase-field-allen-cahn-stationary-front]], the interval where $|u_\varepsilon(x)|\le\frac12$ has width
$$W_\varepsilon=2\sqrt{2\kappa}\,\varepsilon\,\operatorname{artanh}(1/2).$$
If a uniform sample grid has spacing $h>W_\varepsilon$ and the front is centered halfway between two sample points, no grid point lies in that transition interval. This gives a precise unresolved-interface configuration; it is not a sufficient resolution criterion.
items.strategy: Invert the monotone tanh profile at levels ±1/2 and place a uniform grid halfway between sample points.

references.title: Jie Shen and Xiaofeng Yang, Numerical approximations of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems A 28 (2010), 1669–1691
references.locator: §1, printed p. 1670 / PDF p. 2: the authors identify ε as an interfacial-width parameter; the exact profile width and sampling calculation are derived here.

items.title: Modified-energy decay alone does not imply physical-energy decay
items.statement: The scalar inequality $\widetilde E^{1}\le\widetilde E^{0}$, by itself, implies $\mathcal E_{\rm phys}(u^1)\le\mathcal E_{\rm phys}(u^0)$.
items.strategy: Evaluate both energies on explicitly specified one-cell scalar pairs and compare the signs of their changes.

references.title: Jie Shen, Jie Xu, and Jiang Yang, The scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) approach for gradient flows, Journal of Computational Physics 353 (2018), 407–416
references.locator: §3, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2(iv), printed p. 410 / PDF p. 4: the continuous SAV modified-energy law and the note that convergence of the modified numerical energy to the exact energy needs further assumptions. The scalar counterexample is computed here.

items.title: A two-cell Cahn–Hilliard mass and energy ledger
items.statement: Take two unit cells on $(0,2)$, one interior face with transmissibility $T=1$, no-flux boundary faces, $\varepsilon=\kappa=M=\tau=1$, and $u^0=(1,-1)$. The discrete mean is zero, and the one-step convex-splitting state is $u^1=(a,-a)$ where $a$ is the unique root in $(0,1)$ of $2a^3+7a-5=0$. The initial energy is $2$ and the new energy is $2a^2+\frac12(1-a^2)^2<2$.
items.strategy: Reduce the mean-zero two-cell update to one scalar cubic, locate its unique root, and compute both discrete energies exactly.
